ex: They play cricket in the park every Sunday.
Cricket is very popular in India and England.
Do you want to watch a cricket match?
My brother plays cricket for his school team.
cricket.note: As a sport it is uncountable: play cricket. It is also a small insect.

beat.say: dance to the beat · a strong beat
ex: This song has a really great beat.
He makes beats for rappers on his laptop.
Can you hear the beat of the drums?
We danced to the fast beat all night.
beat.note: Most often "beat" is a verb: "Our team beat them 3–0" (won against) or "beat a drum" (hit).

ex: What do you want for dessert tonight?
We had ice cream for dessert yesterday.
She makes a great chocolate dessert on Sundays.
I'm too full to eat any dessert now.
dessert.note: Often no article: "What's for dessert?" Do not confuse with "desert" (a dry, sandy place).

max.say: ten minutes max · up to max
ex: The trip takes twenty minutes max by bus.
We can spend fifty dollars max on the gift.
Turn the heat up to max, please.
Can we invite ten people max to the party?
max.note: Informal short for "maximum": "ten minutes max". "Max" is also a common boy's name.

ex: My brother wants to be a hip-hop artist.
Which hip-hop artist do you listen to most?
The hip-hop artist played three new songs at the concert.
Many young hip-hop artists share their music online.
hip-hop artist.note: Here "artist" means a music performer; "artist" alone often means a painter.

hobby.say: have a hobby · as a hobby
ex: My favorite hobby is taking photos of nature.
Do you have any hobbies in your free time?
She started painting as a hobby last year.
Fishing is a relaxing hobby for many people.

continent.say: on every continent · on the continent

web.say: on the web · search the web
web.note: Also the net a spider makes: "a spider web".

memorial.say: a war memorial · a memorial to sb
memorial.note: Often before a noun: "a memorial service" is a ceremony for someone who died.

publisher.say: a book publisher · a game publisher

insight.say: insight into sth · give an insight

cotton.say: made of cotton · a cotton shirt
ex: This shirt is made of soft cotton.
Cotton is cool and comfortable in summer.
Do you have this dress in cotton?
These socks are one hundred percent cotton.
cotton.note: Uncountable: some cotton, a lot of cotton (not "a cotton").

gay.say: gay people · come out as gay
ex: My brother is gay and lives with his partner.
The city has a big festival for gay people.
Many gay couples live in this part of town.
She told her parents that she is gay.
gay.note: Usually an adjective: "He is gay", "gay people". "A gay" as a noun can sound rude.

discount.say: get a discount · a discount on sth

instrument.say: play an instrument · a musical instrument
ex: Do you play a musical instrument?
The piano is my favorite instrument to play.
She can play three different instruments well.
My son wants to learn a new instrument.
instrument.note: Most often a musical instrument or a device for measuring. A hammer is a "tool", not an "instrument".

debut.say: make your debut · a debut album
ex: This is her debut album, and I love it.
He made his debut in a film last year.
Their debut song was a big hit on the radio.
The young player made her debut for the team today.

GPS.say: turn on the GPS · use GPS

ex: He scored a goal in the last minute.
Our team won the game by two goals.
What a great goal by the young player!
Who scored the first goal of the game?
goal.note: Most often "goal" means an aim: "My goal is to learn English."

massage.say: get a massage · give sb a massage

bicycle.note: "Bike" is more common in everyday speech.

syndrome.say: a rare syndrome · have a syndrome
ex: The doctor said he has a rare syndrome.
This syndrome makes people feel tired all the time.
The doctor explained the syndrome to his parents.
Many children with this syndrome go to regular schools.
The pastor spoke to everyone after the service.
Our pastor visits sick people in the hospital.
She asked the pastor for advice about her family.
The pastor married them in a small church.

yoga.note: Uncountable: do yoga, a yoga class (not "a yoga").

tumor.say: a brain tumor · remove a tumor
ex: The doctors found a small tumor in his brain.
Good news: the tumor is not cancer.
She had surgery to remove the tumor last month.
The tumor grew slowly over many years.

profile.say: on your profile · update your profile
profile.note: Also a short article about a person, or a side view of a face. "High-profile" means well-known.

verdict.say: reach a verdict · a guilty verdict
ex: The jury reached a verdict after two days.
The verdict was "not guilty," and he went home.
Everyone in the room waited quietly for the verdict.
His lawyer was not happy with the verdict.

ego.say: a big ego · hurt sb's ego
ex: His ego is too big to admit his mistakes.
Winning the game was good for her ego.
Don't let your ego stop you from asking for help.
The bad review really hurt his ego.

deadline.say: meet a deadline · miss a deadline

ex: The police found cocaine in his car.
Cocaine is an illegal and very dangerous drug.
He went to prison for selling cocaine.
Many people cannot stop using cocaine without help.
After the operation, he needs careful monitoring for a day.
Air quality monitoring is important in big cities.
The company uses software for network monitoring.
Daily monitoring of the river helps prevent floods.
The company showed a new concept car at the auto show.
This concept car can drive itself without a driver.
Most concept cars never go into real production.
We took photos of the shiny concept car.
concept car.note: A car made to show new ideas and designs; it is usually not sold.

ex: Her name is near the top of the rating list.
The new chess rating list comes out every month.
He moved up twenty places on the rating list.
Check the rating list to see the best players.
rating list.note: Mostly used in chess: a list of players in order of their rating.

ex: This screen has multi-touch, so you can use two fingers.
Multi-touch lets you zoom in on photos with two fingers.
Does this old laptop support multi-touch?
Multi-touch works on most phones and tablets today.
multi-touch.note: Often used before a noun: "a multi-touch screen".

ex: The driver stopped in the pit lane for new tires.
Fans are not allowed to walk in the pit lane.
Cars must drive slowly in the pit lane.
His team made a mistake in the pit lane.
pit lane.note: In car racing, the road next to the track where cars stop for new tires or repairs.

ex: Marijuana is legal in some countries but not here.
Some doctors give medical marijuana to people in pain.
The police found marijuana in his car.
The smell of marijuana filled the whole room.

punk.note: As music it is uncountable; "a punk" is a punk fan. In US slang also a rude young man.

ex: The company hired a consultant to cut costs.
She works as a business consultant in the city.
The consultant gave us some very good advice.
You should ask a tax consultant for help.
consultant.note: A worker who helps you in a store is a "sales assistant", not a "consultant".

ex: He kicked the ball about forty yards.
The store is about a hundred yards from here.
He ran fifty yards in six seconds.
One yard is a little shorter than a meter.
yard.note: Most often "yard" means the land around a house: "The kids play in the yard."

backup.note: Also extra help or a spare: "The police called for backup." "We need a backup plan."

ex: We live about ten minutes from downtown.
Downtown is very busy during the day.
Is there a good, cheap hotel downtown?
Parking downtown is very expensive on weekdays.
downtown.note: American English, often with no "the": "I work downtown." British English says "the town center".

cleaning.note: Uncountable. Also the -ing form of "clean": "She is cleaning the kitchen."

ex: We used a generator when the power went out.
Our generator runs on gas, so buy some more.
Turn on the generator if the lights go off.
The hospital has a big backup generator.
This movie has a very high rating online.
The hotel got a five-star rating from guests.
Always check the ratings before you buy something.
The TV show lost viewers, and its ratings fell.

plus.note: Most often "plus" means "and" or "+": "two plus two", "ten dollars plus tax".

ex: The problem is with the hardware, not the software.
He sells computer hardware and phones online.
Our office needs new hardware this year.
The hardware is old, so the games run slowly.
hardware.note: Uncountable. Also tools and metal things: a "hardware store" sells tools.

ex: He is the new world boxing champ.
The champ won his title fight again tonight.
Hey, champ, you played a great game today!
She has been the chess champ for three years.

baron.note: Also a rich, powerful businessman: "a media baron", "a drug baron".

content.note: Stress CON-tent. Also what is inside: "the contents of a box". Con-TENT means happy.

ex: The server is down, so the site doesn't work.
Our website runs on a fast server.
All your files are saved on the server.
The company bought three new servers this year.
server.note: In the US, a "server" is also a waiter or waitress in a restaurant.

ex: Heroin is a very dangerous and illegal drug.
He was addicted to heroin for many years.
The police found heroin at the border.
She went to a clinic to stop using heroin.
heroin.note: Uncountable. Do not confuse with "heroine" (a female hero).

corridor.note: "Hallway" or "hall" is more common in homes.

ex: The leader built a cult of personality around himself.
In ancient Egypt, there was a cult of the sun god.
Some people say there is a cult of beauty today.
The country had a strong cult of its first king.
cult.note: Most often a strange religious group: "He left the cult." Also "a cult movie" (loved by fans).

feedback.note: Uncountable: some feedback, not "a feedback" or "feedbacks".
